examples.translation: Czy stypendium studenckie można wliczyć do alimentów?

glosses: Créditer (un bon résultat à quelqu'un).
Imputer (un mauvais résultat à quelqu'un).

examples.text: „Das sind Politikfehler, die ihm auch in China klar angerechnet werden“, sagt Nis Grünberg (...) Xi sei offenbar überzeugt gewesen, China werde gegenüber dem Westen als Sieger aus der Pandemie hervorgehen.
examples.translation: « Ce sont des erreurs politiques qui lui sont clairement imputées aussi en Chine », dit Nis Grünberg (...) Xi était apparemment convaincu que la Chine sortirait vainqueur de la pandémie face à l’Occident.

glosses: Facturer.
(in den meisten Fällen positiv) aufnehmen (und in Erinnerung behalten)

examples.text: Man kann es Ihnen gar nicht hoch genug anrechnen, dass Sie so selbstlos geholfen haben.
Und diese Aussage hat man ihm dann als Verrat angerechnet.

glosses: in einer Berechnung mitzählen; als relevant für die Berechnung einer Steuer ansehen

examples.text: Ich kann Ihnen den Gebrauchtwagen mit 500 € auf den Neuwagen anrechnen, wenn Sie wollen.
Das Wohnzimmer kann man sich nicht anteilig als Arbeitszimmer anrechnen lassen.
Sie hat die Kindererziehungsjahre angerechnet bekommen.

translations.source_sense_description: (in den meisten Fällen positiv) aufnehmen (und in Erinnerung behalten)

glosses: To admit the knowledge of; to recognize as a fact or truth; to declare one's belief in.

examples.text: I acknowledge my transgressions.
to acknowledge the being of a god

[T]he charge of my moſt curious, and coſtly ingredients fraide, amounting to ſome ſeaventeene thouſand crovvnes, a trifle in reſpect of health, vvriting your noble name in my Catalogue, I ſhall acknovvledge my ſelfe amply ſatisfi'd.
For ends generally acknowledged to be good.

[N]ow ſuch a liue vngodly, vvithout a care of doing the wil of the Lord (though they profeſſe him in their mouths, yea though they beleeue and acknowledge all the Articles of the Creed, yea haue knowledge of the Scripturs) yet if they liue vngodly, they deny God, and therefore ſhal be denied, […]

Addison: Pathfinder, you're making a mistake.
Ryder: Maybe. But at least I'm willing to acknowledge it.

glosses: To own or recognize in a particular quality, character or relationship; to admit the claims or authority of; to give recognition to.

examples.text: By my soul, I'll ne'er acknowledge thee.
In all thy ways acknowledge Him.

Such an episode in the Island's grand naval story her naval historians naturally abridge; one of them (G.P.R. James) candidly acknowledging that fain would he pass it over did not "impartiality forbid fastidiousness."
He is calmed down only when the bearer of the beard “unbeards,” and acknowledges himself as Asher's old pal: […]

glosses: To be grateful of (e.g. a benefit or a favour)

examples.text: to acknowledge a favor
They his gifts acknowledged none.

glosses: To report (the receipt of a message to its sender).

examples.text: This is to acknowledge your kind invitation to participate in the upcoming debate.

glosses: To own as genuine or valid; to assent to (a legal instrument) to give it validity; to avow or admit in legal form.

examples.text: One who has been sheriff may acknowledge a deed executed by him while in office.

translations.source_sense_description: (in den meisten Fällen positiv) aufnehmen (und in Erinnerung behalten)

glosses: To believe; to put credence in.

examples.text: Someone said there were over 100,000 people there, but I can't credit that.

How shall they credit
 A poor unlearned virgin?
[T]he Heart that is conscious of its own integrity is ever slowest to credit another's Treachery.

She said quite naturally, as if nothing had happened, “I want you to go back home, Victor darling. You mustn’t worry about me any more.”’ Victor told me he could hardly credit it, at first, that she could stand there and say this to him.

glosses: To add to an account.

examples.text: Credit accounts receivable with the amount of the invoice.
For the payroll period credit employees' tips to their wages paid account and debit their minimum wage payable account.
The full amount of the purchase has been credited to your account.

glosses: To acknowledge the contribution of.

examples.text: I credit the town council with restoring the shopping district.
Credit the point guard with another assist.

glosses: To bring honour or repute upon; to do credit to; to raise the estimation of.

examples.text: You credit the church as much by your government as you did the school formerly by your wit.

glosses: Reliance on the truth of something said or done; faith; trust.

examples.text: When Jonathan and the people heard these words they gave no credit into them, nor received them.

glosses: Recognition, respect and admiration.

examples.text: I give you credit for owning up to your mistake.
He arrived five minutes late, but to his credit he did work an extra ten minutes at the end of his shift.

John Gilpin was a citizen
 Of credit and renown,
 A train-band Captain eke was he
 Of famous London town.

The admirable smoothness of the riding also reflected the greatest credit on those who, despite the difficulties caused by the shortage of men and materials, have succeeded in maintaining the track in such first-class order.
"I've got to give credit to Van Persie, it was a great goal. We didn't mean to give them chances but they're a good team."

You have to give director Colm McCarthy, a Scottish TV veteran making his feature film debut, and writer Mike Carey, adapting his own novel, credit for attempting the seemingly impossible task of doing something new with the zombie subgenre.

glosses: Acknowledgement of a contribution, especially in the performing arts.

examples.text: She received a singing credit in last year's operetta.

glosses: Written titles and other information about the TV program or movie shown at the beginning and/or end of the TV program or movie.

examples.text: They kissed, and then the credits rolled.

glosses: A privilege of delayed payment extended to a buyer or borrower on the seller's or lender's belief that what is given will be repaid.

examples.text: In view of your payment record, we are happy to extend further credit to you.

glosses: The time given for payment for something sold on trust.

examples.text: a long credit or a short credit

glosses: A person's credit rating or creditworthiness, as represented by their history of borrowing and repayment (or non payment).

examples.text: What do you mean my credit is no good?

glosses: An addition to certain accounts; the side of an account on which payments received are entered.
A reduction in taxes owed, or a refund for excess taxes paid.

examples.text: Didn't you know that the IRS will refund any excess payroll taxes that you paid if you use the 45(B) general business credit?

glosses: A source of value, distinction or honour.

examples.text: That engineer is a credit to the team.
I published, because I was told I might please such as it was a credit to please.

glosses: A unit of currency used in a fictional universe or timeframe.

examples.text: To repair your star cruiser will cost 100,000 credits.
Aside from the fact that she means nearly ten million credits investment, which no one will insure on this trip, there will necessarily be seventy-three men aboard.

The standard credit was established by the Citadel's Unified Banking Act as the currency of interstellar trade. The credit has a managed floating exchange rate, calculated in real time by the central bank to maintain the average value of all participating currencies. Some regional currencies are worth more than a credit and some less.
"First the Patrons wipe-out our home world, now you blow any chance of us making any credits," Kane said in his gruff sinking voice.

glosses: A nominal unit of value assigned outside of a currency system.

examples.text: Would you like to play? I put in a dollar and I've got two credits left.
Facebook Credits are a virtual currency used only on Facebook that debuted in May 2009. Ten credits are equal to one dollar. Facebook keeps 30% of all Facebook Credit transactions.

glosses: Recognition for having taken a course (class).

examples.text: If you do not come to class, you will not get credit for the class, regardless of how well you do on the final.

glosses: A course credit, a credit hour – used as measure if enough courses have been taken for graduation.

examples.text: Dude, I just need 3 more credits to graduate – I can take socio-linguistics of Swahili if I want.

translations.source_sense_description: (in den meisten Fällen positiv) aufnehmen (und in Erinnerung behalten)

glosses: Aplicar o asignar una función, cargo o distinción.

examples.text: Se le atribuyó la Cruz de Hierro.

glosses: Dar a alguien por autor de un hecho, sin tener pruebas fehacientes para ello.
Dar por reales virtudes o defectos de las cosas, sin tener pruebas fehacientes para ello.

examples.text: A esta planta se le atribuye ser un remedio para el cáncer.

glosses: Señalar o asignar la competencia exclusiva de una función.

examples.text: El juez le atribuyó la patria potestad.

translations.source_sense_description: (in den meisten Fällen positiv) aufnehmen (und in Erinnerung behalten)

glosses: Considerar que algo o alguien tiene valor; reconocer su mérito o importancia.
Establecer el precio de algo, señalar o determinar cuánto vale.
Aumentar el valor o precio de algo.
Establecer con exactitud cuáles son los compuestos de una disolución, y en qué proporción se encuentran.

translations.source_sense_description: (in den meisten Fällen positiv) aufnehmen (und in Erinnerung behalten)

glosses: Homologar o dar validez académica en un país o institución a estudios aprobados en otro país o institución.

examples.text: Qusiera convalidar mi título de médico obtenido en Argentina en España.

glosses: Confirmar, ratificar o dar validez.

examples.text: La Corte Suprema convalidó el polémico derecho a portar armas.

En las cuentas, poner en el debe.
Procesar el ordenador un programa para ponerlo al uso y disposición por parte del usuario.
Tener una sílaba mayor intensidad o mayor duración.
Embestir con ímpetu contra el enemigo o enemigos.
